cwn_entry.cwn_title: k7 0.9.0: record and replay CLI outputs
cwn_entry.cwn_what:
I'm happy to announce the release of [k7 0.9.0](https://github.com/samoht/ocaml-k7) a small tool to record and replay CLI animations.
It's available on MacOS and Linux with ~brew~:
#+begin_example brew install samoht/tap/k7 #+end_example
or in opam:
#+begin_example opam install k7 #+end_example
The main feature vs. other similar tools is that it can use cram tests as input or output, so you can 1/ convert any cram test into an svg file; and 2/ ensure the svg that you use in your README files stays up-to-date with your code.
Apart from this it's in pure OCaml with no browser or ffmpeg involved; it plays ~.cast~ and ~.tape~ files (from ~asciinema~ and ~vhs~) and write ~.cast~ files, but probably has fewer options than those tools, so feel free to open [an issue](https://github.com/samoht/ocaml-k7/issues) if you find anything missing or not working.
See more details in my post: https://gazagnaire.org/blog/2026-10-26-k7.html

Over the summer, @NatKarmios worked on ~dune~ for his internship at [Ahrefs](ahrefs.com). He got [a couple of PRs merged into dune](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pulls?q=is%3Apr+author%3ANatKarmios). Then he wrote a new backend for traces and a matching perfetto extension.
All of the details in his blog post: [Tracing Dune, with a side of graphs](https://tech.ahrefs.com/tracing-dune-with-a-side-of-graphs-56603d7794bc)
TL;DR: you get a graph view of the build, some SQL querying capabilities, it scales to handle Ahrefs' monorepo
We're using the new tracing capability internally. And we're planning on upstreaming it too.

cwn_entry.cwn_title: console: making OCaml CLI tools look good!
cwn_entry.cwn_what:
I'm happy to announce the release of [console 0.9.0](https://github.com/samoht/ocaml-console), a set of widgets for building nice-looking command-line tools. The main design constraint I tried to follow is that the output should look good both for a human at an interactive terminal and for scripts run in CI or other non-interactive loops (like LLM agents). Live rows are redrawn in place and everything useful the program printed is still there when it ends; piped output tries to be relatively clean.
#+attr_html: :width 80% https://us1.discourse-cdn.com/flex020/uploads/ocaml/original/2X/2/21b202a69ab6ff219fa5fee2416d438bbae78d14.gif
You can use it with:
#+begin_example opam install console console-eio #+end_example
The widgets in ~console~ are pure; ~console-eio~ is the driver that runs animations. There are a few limitation (including limited Windows support) but you can already use it to encode quite complex UX. For instance, here a few imitations of package manager frontends using console (recorded using [k7](https://gazagnaire.org/blog/2026-10-26-k7.html)):

You can read more (including how it compares with notty, progress and printbox, here): https://gazagnaire.org/blog/2026-11-02-console.html.
Feedback is very welcome before 1.0, on the [issue tracker](https://github.com/samoht/ocaml-console/issues) or here.

I'm happy to announce a new release of imguiml, the OCaml bindings to Dear ImGui.
- Project page: https://github.com/let-def/imguiml - Documentation: https://let-def.github.io/imguiml
I am taking over maintenance of the project from its original author, Emilien Lemaire.
What's new:
- Updated to *Dear ImGui 1.93.0*, with docking support. - The bindings now work on *arm64* (and probably s390). - Fonts are now rendered with the system *FreeType* instead of ~stb_truetype~, providing higher-quality rendering and better compatibility with modern font formats. - ImGui is now built with support for 32-bit characters, so *Emojis* are supported.
Disclaimer: "Claude" was used in this port, notably to rebase onto the latest version of ImGui and to fix the build on arm64.

We're happy to announce a new alpha release of Introcaml, an extension of OCaml that brings polymorphic printing. It allows printing and inspecting values of any type, without writing printer functions. See the [first announcement](https://discuss.ocaml.org/t/ann-introcaml-alpha-polymorphic-printing-and-introspection-for-ocaml/18407) for an introduction.
Introcaml is developed at [Shogan.ai](https://shogan.ai).
This release ports Introcaml to OCaml 5.5.2. To try it:
#+begin_example opam switch create 5.5.2+introcaml #+end_example
*** What's new
**** JSON printer
A generic JSON printer is available in ~Introspect.Json.*~, intended for debugging (and piping through [jq](https://jqlang.org/) :sweat_smile:):
#+begin_src ocaml # Introspect.Json.to_channel stdout [ `Point {x = 5; y = 0}; `String "foo"; `List [Result.Ok true; Result.Error false] ];; [{"Point":{"x":5,"y":0}},{"String":"foo"},{"List":[{"Ok":true},{"Error":false}]}] - : unit = () # #+end_src
**** Debugging flags
- ~-dblock-desc~ shows descriptors in ~-dlambda~ and similar output. - ~-verbose~ reports descriptor collisions at link time.
*** Compatibility
Object files and executables (exec, cmo, cma, cmx, cmxa, cmxs) now use Introcaml-specific magic numbers (~Caml1999?901~). cmi, cmt and ast files keep the upstream format.
**** js_of_ocaml support
Although this was done in the js_of_ocaml repository, I think it is relevant to point the work we did @hhugo to bring full compatibility with Introcaml. js_of_ocaml can now be installed in Introcaml switches and javascript builds can now be instrumented. This brings polymorphic printing to OCaml programs compiled with js_of_ocaml, at no observable runtime cost (in our experiments).
There is also opt-in integration with the browser's JavaScript console (~console.log~) and debugger, though this appears to be Chrome-only as far as I can tell. See [how to enable it](https://discuss.ocaml.org/t/ann-js-of-ocaml-wasm-of-ocaml-6-5/18632/3).
*** Bug fixes
- *Descriptor collisions:* descriptors are hashed better, reducing collisions. When they still collide, values are printed raw instead of with the wrong names. - *Descriptor representation:* the representation is simpler and more portable. - *Missing descriptors:* I fixed a few cases where descriptors were omitted or lost during compilation (large native allocations, ~#load~ in the toplevel). - *Float arrays and records:* this fixes bugs reported by @vouillon ([#5](https://github.com/let-def/ocaml/issues/5), [#6](https://github.com/let-def/ocaml/issues/6), [#7](https://github.com/let-def/ocaml/issues/7)), paving the way toward compatibility with wasm_of_ocaml. - *Printing:* ~~steps~ now bounds long lists and arrays, and printing is domain-safe.
Introcaml also received the "Claude treatment" to catch bugs I missed :clown_face:.

Hi all!
~ocaml-ssl~ version [0.8.1](https://github.com/savonet/ocaml-ssl/releases/tag/v0.8.1) was just released and added to the ~opam~ registry.
[Version 0.8.0](https://github.com/savonet/ocaml-ssl/releases/tag/v0.8.0/) was released a few weeks back with a bunch of bugfixes and cleanups and 0.8.1 now also adds support for SSL v4.
All projects using ~ocaml-ssl~ should now consider updating to this latest version.
As usual, feel free to suggest patches and etc. Also, the package could definitely use more workforce is you're interested in stepping in.
Thanks,
\-- Romain
